rationale_highlights: W.J.'s life from birth until now provides a case study demonstrating why the Supreme Court of Canada reasoned as it did in Ipeelee.
Almost the whole of his life has been a tragedy when it is measured against the life of almost all other Canadians.
Were it not for the extent to which I find the principles expressed in Ipeelee to have application, I would sentence W.J. to a term of incarceration in the four-year range requested by the Crown.
in light of my reading of Ipeelee, in the context of this case, I sentence W.J. to be incarcerated for a term of two years, ten months.
